content.overview: IDA ss. 22–24 — Prohibition of strikes and lock-outs (IDA ss. 22-24). Complete Labour treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study:
Topic at a glance
CURRENT-LAW UPGRADE — The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 is in force from 21 November 2025. For current disputes, replace the historical IDA ss. 22–24 framework with IR Code ss. 62–64: notice/prohibition rules, illegality, and prohibition on financial aid to illegal strikes or lock-outs. Distinguish statutory illegality from protected/regulated industrial action and test the timing of notice, conciliation, Tribunal/arbitration proceedings, and operative settlements or awards.

IDA ss. 22–24 — Prohibition of strikes and lock-outs (IDA ss. 22-24) is a registered section in Labour & Industrial Law. IDA ss. 22–24 — Prohibition of strikes and lock-outs (IDA ss. 22-24) is governed by Industrial Relations Code, 2020 (in force from 21 November 2025); Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 and other earlier enactments are historical/concordance sources where the applicable transition regime requires them. identify the statute actually in force for the dispute, the date of termination or wage liability, the appropriate Government and the conciliation or reference stage.

Provenance, purpose and doctrinal foundation
The topic exists to organise a legally enforceable rule, doctrine or professional procedure. Read the statutory text, constitutional setting, institutional purpose and binding authorities together. The correct analysis begins with the legal question and avoids replacing the governing enactment with a generic textbook summary.

1. Identify the governing enactment, section, article, rule, doctrine or professional standard named by the topic.
2. Deconstruct definitions, conditions precedent, exceptions, provisos, explanations, jurisdictional limits and remedies.
